message:
Prayagraj, 1858: months after the 1857 revolt, eight villages were taken to build a new Civil Lines.
That is why so many old Indian cities, from Delhi and Nagpur to Jaipur, Kanpur and Jhansi, still have a neighbourhood called Civil Lines with the widest, greenest roads in town.
The British planned these cities as three separate towns: the old city, the cantonment for soldiers, and Civil Lines for the officers who ran the district, with big bungalows on large walled plots.
In Delhi, Civil Lines housed the officials until New Delhi was built. The Viceroy moved out in 1930.
Did you grow up near a Civil Lines? Which city?
